title: ACC Gated Coordination Workflow
trigger: Discipline authoring is complete for the coordination cycle and internal checks have passed.

steps.action: Validate model intake and pre-coordination QA, then place the coordination copy in the governed information state permitted for coordination use. This technical publication or state transition is not formal-exchange authorization or acceptance for downstream reliance.
Run automated clash detection, apply governed exclusions, and triage candidate issues.

Review, prioritize, assign, and date coordination issues within the governed coordination scope. Issue creation, assignment, review, or closure does not constitute authorization for formal exchange or acceptance for declared use.

Remediate authoring issues, republish coordination-use models, and independently verify resolutions. Verification establishes coordination evidence only within the declared scope and does not create formal acceptance authority.

Close or waive verified milestone coordination issues and execute the governed coordination_signoff decision. Record its scope, authorized role or delegation, authority basis, exceptions, and evidence; then declare the package coordination-ready for the separate S7 formal-exchange process. Coordination sign-off shall not itself authorize formal exchange, establish acceptance for declared use, approve a project milestone outside the coordination scope, or establish handover acceptance.
outputs: coordination exception or waiver record where applicable

decision_boundary.meaning: Gate E concludes the governed S5 coordination cycle only.
does_not_establish: milestone_approval outside the explicitly governed coordination scope
decision_boundary.handoff: S7 shall resolve any subsequent formal-exchange authorization, receiving-party acceptance, reliance, milestone, or handover decision under the applicable authority basis.

governance_notes: ACC issue status, issue closure, review completion, folder placement, publication action, transmittal preparation, platform permission, or CDE information-state transition is evidence or execution only and does not create decision authority.
The actor executing a technical ACC action may differ from the actor authorized to make the underlying governed decision; the decision record shall preserve that distinction.

Where the project RACI or other governing authority basis delegates coordination_signoff away from the default Project BIM Manager implementation role, the authorized delegation governs and shall be traceable.
Unresolved authority for a required decision shall remain unresolved and shall not be inferred from ACC permissions, workflow ownership, or role title.

provenance.migration_note: Tool-specific ACC implementation retained below the tool-agnostic L4 S5 doctrine. Curator reconciliation separates coordination_signoff from formal-exchange authorization, acceptance for declared use, milestone approval, and handover acceptance; technical ACC actions do not create authority.
